scope: Layer 1: tokens and themes (T1-T6) for web: packages/styles (foundation, semantics, personalization axes, the four themes), the Tailwind and shadcn bridges, and Figma parity. Swift/iOS parity is out of scope this round (iOS backlog).
notes: Same subjects as round 2. Static re-read of packages/styles on main f7e5e419 plus the generated Figma model (node read of generated/atom63.figma-sync.json); browser tests were not re-run in this review. Since round 2, #315 (a63a96a1) added the rescope rules ([data-a63-brand], [data-a63-surface] re-declare the mode roles through --a63-if-light/--a63-if-dark), #336/#341 made the chart palette brand-safe, tested and carried per brand into Figma, and #323 added the display-hero role. r2-tokens-1 and r2-tokens-6 are fixed; r2-tokens-4 is fixed for its nested-brand half and carried for its theme-only half. Line numbers cite the current files.

scores.evidence: Root combinations resolve and are tested (contrast.browser.test.ts:167-201 at the root, :205-231 in a nested theme+mode scope; figma-parity.browser.test.ts:267-279 now also covers the chart series per brand). Nested brand-only and surface-only scopes now re-declare every mode role (semantics.css:491-832) and are tested (contrast.browser.test.ts:334-405). Gap still open: --a63-status-{info,success,warning,danger}-foreground are relative colours declared in the light block (semantics.css:253-283) and in the brand/surface rescope (:744-770), but the dark block (semantics.css:441-453) re-declares status-* and -subtle without -foreground. A nested [data-a63-mode='dark'] scope (UIProvider mode="dark", provider.tsx:72) therefore inherits a foreground computed from step 600 while the fill moves to step 500.

Declared pairs (contrast.browser.test.ts:12-80) pass in every theme, mode, brand and nested scope. Fixed since r2: chart series are now derived from the brand hue at fixed lightness (semantics.css:291-295, :456-460) and chart-palette.browser.test.ts:118-162 asserts 3:1 against page and panel for every theme x mode x brand. Still undeclared and failing: the status solid-fill pair (--a63-status-*-foreground on --a63-status-*) is in no pair list (contrast.browser.test.ts:49-58 lists status accents against the page only), and it drops to about 3.4:1 (info) and 3.9:1 (danger) in a nested dark scope (see T1). Category palette pairs (-subtle-foreground on -subtle, rule 9 of AGENTS.md) are not declared either (grep 'category' in contrast.browser.test.ts finds nothing). Four token-role entries remain baselined with no inverse-surface token (craft-baseline.json:16-19).

Dead tokens are still not checked: check-token-economy.mjs:45 only collects --theme-/--gel- tokens, prefixes nothing declares. The 40 --a63-badge-<hue>-accent/-foreground tokens are now declared three times (contracts/badge.css:10, :53, :98, the third copy added by the rescope) and still read by nothing (badge.css:25 reads --badge-bg; grep 'a63-badge-[a-z]*-accent' in packages/ui-react/src finds no reader). Component-tier tokens (--a63-alert-background, --a63-control-outline-*) still sit in the semantic layer (semantics.css:701-711), and --a63-surface-sidebar/--a63-surface-recessed still equal each other in both modes (semantics.css:142-144, :369-370, :598-601).

Radius is one multiplier ramp (foundation/radius.css:12-37) and density scales space and control heights by one unit (density.browser.test.ts). The type scale is still not monotonic: --typography-10xl-font-size stays 40px at every width (foundation/typography.css:47, :163, :200) while 9xl is 44px at 640px and 49px at 768px (:71, :94), so the display role (type-roles.css:39, 10xl) is smaller than 9xl on tablet and desktop. The new display-hero role clamps from 10xl (type-roles.css:22-26), so it inherits the same floor. The stale comment remains: foundation/radius.css:29 says --radius-full is 2x md while :32 computes 2x xl.

Figma parity passes for every synced variable (figma-parity.browser.test.ts compares every axis mode and every theme x brand x surface x mode colour; chart series now carried per brand through splitBrandByMode, generate-figma-sync.mjs:737-800, asserted at figma-parity.browser.test.ts:271-279). Not 4: 64 'computed' variables, including --a63-text-primary (varies on brand, mode, surface, theme) and the control heights, still show Figma their default only (atom63.figma-sync.json summary and computed list). Swift n/a this round (iOS backlog).
n/a: scored under the 'Personalization axes' (brand) and 'Theme authoring' subjects.

subjects.subject: Personalization axes (brand, surface, surface tint, radius, type scale, density, font, mode)

scores.evidence: Fixed since r2 (r2-tokens-1): a brand-only or surface-only scope now re-declares the brand and neutral roles (focus ring :722-723, text accent :644-645, selection, choice cards, tinted surfaces) keyed to the nearest mode scope (semantics.css:491-832), aqua and terminal do the same (aqua.css:178-179, terminal.css:192-193), and contrast.browser.test.ts:339-405 resolves them against a reference that sets the mode. personalization-axes.md:72 now describes this correctly. Still open: radius and type scale do nothing on a nested scope because the --radius-* ramp and --typography-* sizes are computed on :root (foundation/radius.css:12-37; typography.css:18-49), while radius.css:12-14 and type-scale.css:7-10 say a subtree can override them; story-probes.tsx:111 still works around it ('it FREEZES to the root multiplier'). UIProvider mode="system" still stamps light whatever the OS preference (provider.tsx:65).

Six brands x four themes x two modes pass the brand pairs (contrast.browser.test.ts:237-300), and the same pairs now pass inside nested brand-only and surface-only scopes (:368-405). Per-brand contrast exceptions remain documented in brand-action.css.

Attributes follow data-a63-<axis>. Legacy aliases remain: density is still matched as ':is([data-a63-density], [data-density])' (the Figma model skips 32 tokens under that exact scope, atom63.figma-sync.json skipped list), and the .dark/.light classes sit beside data-a63-mode (semantics.css:95-97, :330).

Radius multipliers 0/0.5/1/1.5 (radius.css:21-39) and type-scale 0.9/1/1.1/1.2 (type-scale.css:12-26) are tested in personalization-axes.browser.test.ts; compact density is one 0.875 unit (density.browser.test.ts). Density still does not reach Tailwind spacing (see the Tailwind bridge subject).

Figma has one collection per axis with matching modes (14 collections, 1167 variables in the atom63.figma-sync.json summary); the 128 rescope declarations are skipped as 'context scope: [data-a63-brand], [data-a63-surface]' by design, since Figma's Brand and Surface collections already vary those values. The 'auto' brand is skipped by design.

Adding a brand is documented (theme-authoring.md:78-117) and check-theme-authoring.mjs:56 (brandListProblems) fails while a hand-written brand list disagrees. Polish: the hand-written lists still have to be edited by hand.

Contrast and parity pass for modern at the root, in a nested theme+mode scope and in nested brand/surface scopes (contrast.browser.test.ts:167-231, :339-405). Polish: the dark widget face rule [data-a63-theme='modern']:is(.dark,[data-a63-mode='dark']) (modern.css:47) still has no descendant form.
All declared pairs pass for modern/light and modern/dark (contrast.browser.test.ts:167-231).
Assigns contract hooks only (modern.css:16-46).

Unchanged since r2. The new-theme checklist (theme-authoring.md:63-76) names the resolver and the path in check-theme-authoring.mjs, which hard-codes four themes (check-theme-authoring.mjs:16-21). Theme ids are still hand-listed in themes/index.css:1-4, contrast.browser.test.ts:9, chart-palette.browser.test.ts:13 (new since r2), the figma parity test, generate-figma-sync.mjs and ui-react theme options. Every block is @theme inline, so utilities emit var(--a63-*) and follow nested scopes; roles are generated from roles.json (check:roles). New display-hero utilities read the role tokens (theme.css:624-640).
check:craft token-role reads roles.json, so a fill token used as text is flagged in TSX. The status -foreground utilities inherit the nested-dark gap from the semantic layer.

Still reuses Tailwind's names with other values: text-6xl is 28px (foundation/typography.css:39) against Tailwind's 60px; rounded-full is a pill (theme.css:517-519) while the CSS variable --radius-full is a soft 2x xl corner (foundation/radius.css:32). The display steps are now exposed as role utilities (text-display, theme.css:636), which softens the 10xl/11xl gap.

theme.css still defines no --spacing (grep '^\s*--spacing' in theme.css finds nothing), so p-*, gap-* and m-* use Tailwind's fixed 0.25rem and ignore [data-a63-density]; templates lay out with these utilities.

Parity holds for what is synced, but the designer-visible skips remain: 60 phone form-factor tokens ('context scope: [data-a63-form-factor=*]'), 32 density-scoped tokens, 7 coarse-pointer and 4 reduced-motion conditionals (atom63.figma-sync.json skipped list, 412 skipped in all, of which 128 are the by-design brand/surface rescope). findings.subject: Personalization axes (brand, surface, surface tint, radius, type scale, density, font, mode)
findings.summary: Carried from r2-tokens-2: on a nested scope the radius and type-scale axes do nothing, although the source comments say a subtree can override them.
findings.evidence: foundation/radius.css:12-37 and foundation/typography.css:18-49 compute the ramps on :root; radius.css:12-14 and type-scale.css:7-10 promise subtree overrides; packages/ui-react/src/components/story-probes.tsx:111 works around it.
findings.fix: Re-declare the computed --radius-* and --typography-* ramps on [data-a63-radius] and [data-a63-type-scale] (as density does), and add a nested-scope assertion to personalization-axes.browser.test.ts.

findings.subject: Theme: aqua
findings.summary: Carried from r2-tokens-3: a nested mode-only scope inside aqua, or a theme-only aqua scope under an html-class mode, loses aqua's mode-split surfaces.
findings.evidence: packages/styles/src/themes/aqua.css:112, :134 (same-element only; compare terminal.css:94, :152); contrast.browser.test.ts:211-213 always sets theme and mode together.
findings.fix: Add the descendant forms ([data-a63-theme='aqua'] :is(.dark,[data-a63-mode='dark'])) and a nested mode-only contrast case.

findings.subject: Theme: terminal
findings.summary: Narrowed from r2-tokens-4: <UIProvider theme="terminal"> without a mode on the same element (mode from the html class) gets the CRT glow over neutral text and surfaces. The nested-brand half is fixed.
findings.evidence: packages/styles/src/themes/terminal.css:93-94, :151-152 require the mode on the theme element or a descendant; terminal.css:192-193 now covers nested brand/surface.
findings.fix: Key the phosphor palette to an ancestor mode too (:is(.dark,[data-a63-mode='dark']) [data-a63-theme='terminal']) or through --a63-if-light/--a63-if-dark, and test a theme-only nested scope.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: Carried from r2-tokens-5: --a63-status-*-foreground is not re-declared in the dark block, so a solid info or danger fill in a nested dark scope gets near-white text at about 3.4:1, and the pair is not declared.
findings.evidence: packages/styles/src/tokens/semantics.css:253-283 (light), :441-453 (dark block without -foreground), :744-770 (rescope has them); contrast.browser.test.ts:49-58 has no status fill/foreground pair.
findings.fix: Emit the four -foreground relative colours in the dark block too, and add { fg: status-*-foreground, bg: status-* } to the pair lists.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: Carried from r2-tokens-7: dead tokens are not checked; the badge accent tokens nothing reads are now declared three times.
findings.fix: Extend the unused scan to --a63-* (multiline-aware, packages and apps), baseline what is intentionally public, and delete the unread badge tokens.

findings.subject: Foundation and semantic tokens (packages/styles/src/tokens)
findings.summary: Carried from r2-tokens-8: the type scale is not monotonic; 10xl (display) is a fixed 40px, below 9xl's 44px and 49px at 640px and 768px.
findings.fix: Give 10xl and 11xl responsive steps above 9xl at each breakpoint, or drop 9xl's growth, and add a monotonicity assertion.

findings.subject: Tailwind bridge (packages/styles/src/tailwind)
findings.summary: Carried from r2-tokens-9: density does not reach Tailwind spacing utilities, so compact density tightens components but not template layout.
findings.fix: Set --spacing in the bridge to a density-scaled unit (calc(0.25rem * var(--a63-density-scale))).

findings.subject: Tailwind bridge (packages/styles/src/tailwind)
findings.summary: Carried from r2-tokens-10: the bridge keeps Tailwind's names with other values (text-6xl is 28px), and rounded-full (a pill) and --radius-full (a soft corner) mean two things.
findings.fix: Document the mapping on the Tailwind docs page and steer to role utilities, or rename --radius-full.

findings.subject: shadcn bridges (compat/shadcn.css, compat/a63-from-shadcn.css)
findings.summary: Carried from r2-tokens-11: shadcn aliases are declared only on mode scopes, so inside a brand- or surface-only UIProvider --primary, --ring and --background now disagree with the re-declared --a63-* roles.
findings.fix: Add [data-a63-brand], [data-a63-surface] and [data-a63-theme] to the generated alias selector.

findings.subject: shadcn bridges (compat/shadcn.css, compat/a63-from-shadcn.css)
